newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO TAKE DECISIVE STEP TOWARDS FRENCH CROWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO TAKE DECISIVE STEP TOWARDS FRENCH CROWN.

text.p: Monaco took a decisive step towards their first French league crown for a decade when they beat neighbours Nice 2-0 on Wednesday to move 10 points clear of nearest rivals Paris St Germain.
PSG, beaten 2-1 in a thrilling match against champions Auxerre, admitted their title hopes were now very slim.

"We only hope to keep our second place and to beat Liverpool in the Cup Winners' Cup semifinals. Given Monaco's qualities, it would be preposterous to say we have a chance of the title," said Paris coach Joel Bats.
Monaco had to fight harder than expected at bottom-of-the-table Nice.

They were fortunate to take the lead with an own goal by Nice striker Franck Potier in the 12th minute and had to wait until injury time for Nigeria's Viktor Ikpeba to seal victory with a second goal.
Monaco coach Jean Tigana said: "Anything can still happen in the title race. But I admit we feel better right now. We took yet another step towards it." .
Antoine Sibierski broke the deadlock in the tense Auxerre-PSG clash with a goal in the 33rd minute.
Benoit Cauet equalised shortly before the break but Auxerre's pressure paid off in the 50th minute when Bernard Diomede scored following a corner. He hit the post late in the game.
Two of the other title contenders, Bordeaux and Nantes, drew 0-0 on Tuesday, allowing Strasbourg, who beat Caen 2-0 on Wednesday, to move back to third, two points behind PSG.
David Zitelli, the first division's top marksman, scored his 19th goal of the season -- Strasbourg's second -- in the 80th minute.
Former European champions Marseille ended a four-game losing streak with a 4-1 victory over Nancy.
